subject: Observability: retention profiles, tracing fees & dashboard seat pricing

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability: retention profiles, tracing fees & dashboard seat pricing

Hi John,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — really appreciate the walkthrough of your telemetry and how you use traces for incident triage. I promised to send a concise set of packaging options for the observability add-ons you asked about (trace retention, long-term storage for traces/metrics, and the advanced dashboard seats).

Attached is a spreadsheet with three scenario bundles (Base, Extended, and Enterprise) and a separate sheet that breaks out per-GB retention pricing and per-seat dashboard fees. High level:
- Base: 30-day trace retention, 10GB/day ingestion retention tier, 5 advanced dashboard seats included
- Extended: 90-day trace retention, 50GB/day tier, 15 seats + reduced per-GB rate
- Enterprise: custom retention beyond 90 days, footprint discounts, priority support

Two clarifying points I want your input on before we lock numbers:
1) Do you expect spikes >100GB/day during peak jobs? That would push you into the next ingest tier.
2) Will all dashboard seats be centralized (product analytics team) or spread across engineering teams (we usually price differently when seats are distributed).

If helpful I can convert the Extended scenario into a blended, piecewise quote that mixes committed retention capacity with overage rates — that tends to be attractive for customers who are early in their observability journey.

Next step: if you send me expected daily GB and approximate number of seats by team, I can produce a line-item quote and a 30-day trial plan for the Extended bundle.

Cheers,

Priyom Das

From: john.matthews@acme-analytics.com

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability: retention profiles, tracing fees & dashboard seat pricing

Thanks Priyom — helpful summary and clear options. A few quick answers and follow-ups: 

- Spikes: yes, during batch replays we see bursts up to ~140GB/day for a 2–3 day window. Otherwise baseline is ~18GB/day.
- Seats: about 8 seats for central product analytics and 6 for engineering (so 14 total, distributed across two "teams").

Questions: 
1) You mentioned "blended, piecewise quote" — can you share an example of how that would look for us? I want something that caps our predictable monthly spend but doesn't penalize short replays.
2) For Enterprise retention beyond 90 days, can you confirm whether traces retained beyond 90 days are still searchable with the same SLA, or do they move to an "archive" index with longer query latency?
3) Do the dashboard seats include custom widget development (one-off)? We may want a couple of bespoke visualizations.

If you can get an adapted quote early tomorrow I can loop in procurement (should be quick once we have unit economics).

Best,
John
John Matthews
Director, Observability & Platform
Acme Analytics

From: camila.reyes@redwood.ai
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Observability: retention profiles, tracing fees & dashboard seat pricing

Priyom / Ben — forwarding John's replies. He gave concrete numbers on baseline vs spikes and seat distribution. Proposed approach:

- Build a piecewise pricing schedule: commit to a 25GB/day retention tier (covers baseline) + burst buffer up to 150GB/day billed at a reduced overage rate for bursts that last <= 72 hours. That yields predictable MRR and keeps short replays affordable.
- Seats: price first 10 seats at list, additional seats tiered at 30% off list if committed as a package. Offer 2 free "custom widget" hours as part of Extended bundle; additional dev hours are scoped separately.
- Traces >90 days: for Enterprise we keep them in hot storage with the same search SLA (we'll push customers to that tier and require a minimum commit). Otherwise archive mode moves to cold storage with query latency up to 10x.

Concession idea: for RDW-4782, if Acme commits to 12 months on Extended bundle we can offer a one-time 15% discount on the monthly observability add-on (not on core inference). That swaps some margin for predictable revenue and avoids procurement escalation.

Can you draft a one-page quote with those elements and two payment options (monthly vs annual prepay) and I will quick-check before sending to John.

— Camila

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai

John — thanks for the fast turnaround and the details. Per internal alignment, attached here is a single-page quote and a short SOW draft. Highlights:

- Piecewise retention: 25GB/day committed (covers baseline) + burst slab up to 150GB/day billed at $0.03/GB for bursts (versus standard $0.08/GB) limited to 72 hours per incident before falling back to standard overage.
- Seat pricing: first 10 seats $35/seat/month, seats 11–20 $24.50/seat/month (30% off) when committed as a block.
- Dashboard work: 2 'custom widget' hours included; further dev at block rate or runbook-based SOW.
- Enterprise retention: hot storage with same query SLA requires a 12-month Extended bundle commitment.
- Concession: 15% observability add-on discount for 12-month Extended commitment (applies when deal signed and invoice prepay option chosen).

Attachments: Observability_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx (updated), SOW_Retention-Dashboards_v1.docx (SOW draft), one-page-quote-ACME-RDW-4782.pdf (pricing summary).

Next steps: If that aligns, I can (a) send a DocuSign for the SOW + order form and (b) spin up the 30-day Extended trial environment. Which of those should we prioritize for procurement?

Thanks — looking forward to closing this for you.
